*You also need people who are immersed in these environments. Yak herders and fishermen can notice changes in rivers, glaciers and glacial lakes. Yak herders have been the first to report growing glacial lakes during several events. Oral histories with elders can reveal smaller avalanches, glacial-lake floods and other events that science has not recorded, helping identify potential hotspots*.

Climate change, amidst so many other things, is bridging the expert-layman divide which has been a defining feature of positivist natural science. This trend needs to continue where people's knowledge is given due respect in policy making, and is not limited to political rhetoric. 


Nepal floods: The red flags in dam-building in the Himalayashttps://lnkd.in/dNhhHpQw
comment: Local knowledge is often the earliest warning system, but the challenge is creating channels where these observations are systematically captured, validated, and integrated into formal risk models before disasters occur.
